text:
mike: noticing persistent tiny GPU fragments in ap-southeast2 for ~2h, preempt churn up and small jobs queueing.
anya: yup, scheduler logs show repeated preempt->reschedule loops. Hetero GPU memory shapes + aggressive binpack.
ji-ho: quick mitigation idea: add a temporary "frag-escort" label on a small set of nodes and bias scheduler scoring to prefer landing tiny pods there instead of global coalesce.
mike: also scale warm-pool +20% in that AZ for 30m as a fallback.
anya: plan: 1) label 8 nodes: fragment-friendly, 2) apply canary scoring bonus preferFrag=45 to 10% schedulers, 3) patch low-priority ns tolerations with tolerationSeconds=1800.
ji-ho: sample commands (dry-run first):
kubectl label node gpu-apse-0{1..8} frag-friendly=true
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap gpu-scheduler-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"preferFragScore":"45","cohort":"apse-frag-canary"}}'
kubectl -n spot-batch patch deployment --all -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"frag-friendly","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoSchedule","tolerationSeconds":1800}]}}}}'
mike: infra-bot, create runbook and hook fit_failures, preempt_rate, pod_start_latency. Canary window 30m.
scheduler-bot: [runbook] id=rb-apse-01 owner=ji-ho duration=30m.
anya: applied labels and tolerations; canary scoring to 10% schedulers now.
scheduler-bot: [metric] 8m telemetry: preempt_rate -12%, fit_failures -16%, pod_start_p50 -38s.
ji-ho: good early signal. If it holds >20m, expand to 50% and keep warm-pool +20% for 2h.
mike: follow-ups: capture allocation traces (ji-ho), cost delta estimate for warm-pool (anya), RFC for frag-escort heuristic (mike).
anya: note: don't remove labels until we confirm reserved-job tail latency unaffected. Rollback plan ready.
scheduler-bot: [alert] canary expires in 30m unless extended.
